thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU serving cluster 'gpupool-europe-2' queue depth spike detected — queue growth > 1200 reqs, GPU util > 95%, 429 rate rising. Autoscaler attempted 3 scale ops; hit max-pool-size limit. Investigate.

alex: acknowledged. I'm taking on-call. Paging eng-runtime and eng-sre.

jordan: on it — looking at autoscaler logs now. grabbing recent HPA/controller events.

lee: seeing repeated errors in autoscaler: 
```
E[autoscaler] scale denied: pool-size=80, max-pool-size=80
W[tokenbucket] drop: tier=standard token_shortage=1.8s
```
429s correlate with tokenbucket rejects and queue timeouts.

maya: customers_reporting: 3+ teams reporting elevated 429s and timed out chat completions. Support already opened incident tickets for acct: acme-inc, vectra, marketwise.

alex: quick assessment: two issues colliding — hardware cap (max nodes) preventing scale, and token-bucket rate config for 'standard' tier too strict under burst load. Need immediate mitigation to reduce customer impact. Options: 1) temporarily raise max-pool-size (if capacity available in region), 2) loosen token bucket burst/rate, 3) degrade heavy models to smaller variant and route low-priority traffic to best-effort pool, 4) apply emergency throttles by customer/tier to preserve SLO for paid customers.

jordan: checking infra capacity: cloud quotas free? I see spare quota in eu-west-2 but requires infra approval to attach GPUs to gpupool-europe-2; can perform manual node-add via internal autoscaler API if approved.

lee: while jordan checks capacity, we can immediately tune token buckets to reduce hard rejects. Current standard tier token config: rate=120r/s, burst=200. Under long tail we null out KV cache hits and token draw bursts -> big reject. Suggest set rate=80, burst=400 to allow larger bursts but slower steady-state, or alternatively increase refill rate per second. Also lower per-connection concurrency for standard to 4.

alex: agree. mitigation plan: 1) jordan triggers emergency node-add + set pool max to 110 (from 80) if capacity ok. 2) lee patches tokenbin config for standard tier to rate=140, burst=450 (experimentally allowing more bursts while keeping server safe). 3) maya + tom notify the 3 impacted customers and apply per-customer temporary reduced concurrency rule. 4) Create rollback plan and an alert to revert config if error rate rises elsewhere.

jordan: infra can add up to 30 nodes; initiating `internal-autoscaler scale gpupool-europe-2 --set-max 110` now. Command output: 
```
> internal-autoscaler request accepted: increase max-pool-size 80 -> 110
> pending cloud provisioning request id=cp-8942
```
Wait ~2-4min for nodes to show up.

lee: pushing token bucket change to staging-like config then prod: patch snippet: 
```yaml
tiers:
  standard:
    token_rate: 140
    token_burst: 450
    max_concurrency: 4
```
Applying: `kubectl apply -f /ops/configs/tokenbucket-standard.yaml --namespace=gpupools`

alex: applying now. watch logs for reduction in 429s. If 429s drop, keep changes for 30m then iterate to target production rates. If errors increase, rollback.

incident-bot: NOTE: Page created and on-call assigned to alex. Severity: P2->escalate if >50% of paid requests affected. Links: runbook/gpu-saturation, dashboard/gpupool-europe-2.

(50s later)

jordan: cloud nodes provisioned: +20 nodes joined pool; current pool-size=98, util trending down to 78%. Autoscaler still active.

lee: tokenbucket change rolled out to gpupools namespace. Observed token drop rate gone from ~120/s -> ~25/s. 429s dropping in frontend metrics.

maya: support notes: acme-inc reported degraded completions timeouts reduced from 60%->12% after changes. vectra still seeing intermittent 429s for large context jobs; assigned to eng-runtime for per-job routing.

alex: good. Now do targeted mitigations for vectra: route their heavy model to best-effort pool or push to smaller model variant for 10m window. Jordan can we create a route override?

jordan: yes — route rule created: `route: vectra -> gpupool-europe-best-effort for model-xlarge` activated. Confirmed by router logs: vectra traffic shifted. 429s for vectra drop.

tom: quick note for billing/CS: will CSV impacted request counts for acme-inc/vectra/marketwise and post to the customer slack channel + case.

alex: doing quick postmortem action items now: 1) Increase default max-pool-size headroom per region by config or automated quota check, 2) Add autoscaler fallback to smaller model variant when max nodes hit, 3) Review token-bucket defaults per tier (current defaults too brittle for sudden workload shifts), 4) Improve runbook step ordering so tokenbucket tune comes before node-add if cloud is constrained.

incident-bot: HANDOFF: alex -> sara in 25 minutes. Please confirm next steps and keep incidents channel updated.

(switch to handoff 25m later)

sara: taking over on-call. Summary: nodes scaled +20, tokenbucket patched to rate=140/burst=450, vectra routed to best-effort for heavy model, customer notifications sent. Current metrics: overall 429 rate near baseline, queue depth steadily falling. I'll keep monitoring and coordinate post-incident followups with eng-runtime and product.

alex: thanks @sara. leaving details in /incidents/1848735120-thread-notes and created a short playbook PR for tokenbucket emergency tuning.

jordan: created infra change request to auto-bump max-pool-size when spare capacity exists and add safety check for overprovision. Link: infra/CR-4721.

lee: will schedule a proper postmortem doc with graphs and log excerpts (token drop vs 429s vs pool-size) + recommended default param changes.

maya: support will follow up with customers and keep CS looped for any credits or RCAs.

sara: closing this thread for live ops; will re-open if any regressions. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
